title: Active learning maps wind-tunnel terrain equivalence
summary: A learned surrogate selected automated wind-tunnel experiments that mapped terrain configurations with similar second-order wind statistics. Different terrain shapes could meet the study's equivalence criterion. This does not imply identical full turbulence fields or equal structural safety; higher-order statistics can differ. Estimated experiment savings are not a fully executed randomized comparison with alternative sampling.

evidence.tested: Automated terrain changes and measured wind profiles defined experimental equivalence regions.
evidence.unknown: Generality beyond the facility, full-field equivalence and safety outcomes remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process sequential active learning supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary article retrieved via browser request: publication metadata, Gaussian-process Methods and terrain-study Results; supplements not reviewed.
